judge_assessment.explanation: Every rate the judge lists is right and I recomputed all nineteen checks: (8-2)/(4-1)=2; line B through the origin and (8,8) has slope 1; C=4d+7 gives rate 4 and C(3)=19; line A through (0,2) and (4,14) has rate 3; the tub table gives 50-32=18 litres and (32-14)/(5-2)=6 litres per minute; Plan B is 84/6=14 dollars per hour against Plan A's 12; line C through (0,16) and (8,0) has rate -2; the barrel L=-5x+40 has rate -5 and L(6)=10; the nonlinear table gives 2 then 4; Mara runs 15/3=5 m/s against Ben's 4.5; (-5-5)/(2-(-3))=-2; and the final order -5, -2, 3, 6 matches the four rates the synthesis names. The judge's note that the OCR problem-count discrepancy came from table values rather than item numbers is also correct - the tex has exactly twelve \problem calls. What the judge missed is on the grading page and in two stems. The Quick Answers bank prints '6. 14, -' and '10. 5, -': both dashes are compare entries that gate_log.txt records as PASS and that answer_key.tex boxes as '<' and '>', so the two comparison sub-parts - the actual point of a rate-comparison sheet - print as blanks. And two problems attach an explanation to a verified number with no manual entry: problem 7 asks 'Find its rate of change, and say what the sign of your answer means' (verify.json id 7 is a lone slope entry), and problem 9(b) asks the student to 'explain how the two answers show the table is not linear' (id 9 is two slope entries). Only problem 12 carries a manual entry, so the sheet's other two reasoning slots are recorded as machine-verified.

strengths_to_preserve: Figure 1 is drawn once on page 1 and reused by problems 2, 4 and 7, with the stem of each of those problems restating the two lattice points the line passes through ('Line B passes through the origin and through (8, 8)'). The student reads a rate off a graph three times at different difficulties without three redundant grids, and the reused figure is labelled in the stem so the reference cannot be misread.

Problem 9 is the item that makes the sheet more than a slope drill: the table is deliberately not linear, and part (b) requires computing the rate over a second interval (2 then 4) so that non-linearity is demonstrated by the student's own two numbers rather than asserted. verify.json backs it with two separate slope entries.

Units survive into the answers everywhere: '4 dollars per mile', '6 litres per minute', '-5 litres per minute', '5 metres per second', and the key states what the negative sign means in context rather than leaving it as a sign ('the rate of change is -5 litres per minute - the barrel is losing').

Problem 12 does exactly what a synthesis item should: it names the four earlier problems by number (4, 7, 5, 8), asks for their rates in one order, and carries a genuine manual entry in verify.json for the 'which representation was easiest and why' half - the one open response on the sheet that is correctly declared.

root_causes.description: The two comparison sub-parts print as em-dashes because render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds and a relation operator raises, falling through to '---'. The same glyph is what the module uses for manual-only ids, so on a sheet that does contain a manual item (problem 12) the meaning is genuinely ambiguous.
evidence: verify.json id 6 second entry {type: compare, expected: '<'} and id 10 second entry {type: compare, expected: '>'}, both recorded PASS in gate_log.txt.
answer_key.tex line 92 boxes 'Plan A's rate < Plan B's' and line 157 boxes 'Mara's speed > Ben's'.
verify.json id 12 carries a genuine manual entry, so both meanings of '---' are live in this one document.

root_causes.description: Explanation slots that sit beside a verified number are not declared. The author correctly flagged the fully open synthesis half of problem 12 but treated the interpretive halves of problems 7 and 9 as covered by the slope values they accompany, so two reasoning answers are recorded as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7: 'Find its rate of change, and say what the sign of your answer means.' verify.json id 7 is a single slope entry (-2).
worksheet.tex problem 9(b): 'Find the rate of change from x = 2 to x = 4, then explain how the two answers show the table is not linear.' verify.json id 9 is two slope entries (2 and 4).
verify.json's only manual entry is on id 12.

improvements.title: Render the two verified rate comparisons instead of blanking rows 6 and 10
improvements.proposed_change: Handle relation strings in render_quick_answers._fmt before the sympify attempt, printing the operator between the entry's compared values (id 6 -> 'Plan A < Plan B' or at minimum '<'), and reserve '---' for ids whose entries are all manual. Passing the entry rather than entry['expected'] into the formatter makes 'values' available for the rendering.
improvements.regression_test: Render this task's verify.json and assert that rows 6 and 10 each contain a relation operator, while id 12's manual entry still contributes no em-dash of its own (its compare list already prints). Today rows 6 and 10 end in '-', so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The two sub-parts that carry the sheet's stated purpose - comparing rates that arrive in different forms - regain printed answers on the grading page.
improvements.risk: Longer rows; column_count already adapts, so this is cosmetic.

improvements.title: Declare manual entries for the sign interpretation in problem 7 and the non-linearity argument in problem 9(b)
improvements.proposed_change: Add an open-response verb scan to the gate chain so a stem containing 'say what ... means' or 'explain how' forces a manual entry on that id. Here ids 7 and 9 gain manual entries beside their slope checks, matching the treatment problem 12 already receives, so the sheet's three reasoning slots are declared consistently instead of one out of three.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with problem 9's stem and a verify.json id 9 holding two slope entries only. The check must exit non-zero naming the 'explain how the two answers show the table is not linear' slot; adding a manual entry for id 9 makes the fixture pass.
improvements.expected_impact: Problem 9's explanation is the whole point of including a non-linear table; declaring it manual puts the student's argument in front of a reviewer rather than letting two correct slopes imply a correct conclusion.
improvements.risk: Two more manual items on a twelve-problem sheet; the matcher must not fire on the directions block, which contains 'order them on a number line, not by size'.

case_summary: A comprehensive rate-of-change review whose nineteen checks I recomputed in full and found exact, including the negative rates, the deliberately non-linear table, and the four-rate synthesis order. The design is strong: one shared figure on page 1 is reused by three problems at rising difficulty, units survive into every answer, and problem 12 names the four source problems and carries a properly declared manual entry. Two defects survive the ACCEPT. The Quick Answers bank prints '6. 14, -' and '10. 5, -', dropping both verified comparisons - the sub-parts that carry the sheet's declared focus - because _fmt sympifies the relation string and falls back to the manual glyph, which is genuinely ambiguous here since problem 12 is a real manual item. And problems 7 and 9(b) attach an interpretation to a verified number with no manual entry, so two of the sheet's three reasoning slots are recorded as machine-verified while the third is not.
